lew42 framework (Item / List / Page)
summary: The owner's own no-build vanilla-JS object framework. Every saved thing is an Item (id, data, named Lists of child Items); item.set(delta) emits a delta event that bubbles to the root, whose Store writes one nested JSON line per change ({"tasks":{"c3":{"set":{…}}}}) to the root's append-only .jsonl file. Opening replays every line through set(). On the dev machine a recursive fs.watch plus a per-socket byte-offset tailer pushes new lines over one WebSocket per tab; record files are written through one Node entry point (Servex POST /api/item) that applies each line to a live root before appending. No conflict resolution, no sequence numbers, no snapshots; production is static and read-only.
status: in-house, dev-only live sync; integration/data-shapes-2 (9ba46ee, 2026-10-28) ready to merge, not merged
taxonomy_note: taxonomy.md was a skeleton when these ops were written; layers, strategies and features use the draft axis names from the lew42-study brief, to be remapped

layers.what: Item (id, data, set/get, hydrate), List (ordered, evented, id-keyed), Page (an Item with a url), Ref (pointer by path)
delta events bubble up parent links; Store.hops/wrap turn them into one nested line per change
one append-only JSONL file per root, children inline, optional break-out to own folder; files committed to git
Servex record_lines/run_item: validate, apply to a live Node root, appendFileSync; dev-server Append.js as fallback
dev-only WebSocket: subscribe(path, byte offset) -> jsonl frames from Tail.js; jsonl_reset when a file shrinks
browser Store replays lines through set(), skips its own echo by exact text, emits read
Dated collections filed by day with per-day pointer-row index.jsonl; in-memory query process

strategies.value: single-file-truth: one append-only file per root; Node live root validates record writes; browsers apply optimistically
none: file line order decides, last line wins per field, no rebase of optimistic local state; CRDT/merge explicitly rejected
nested JSON op per line: keys are the path (list name, member id), leaf is a method name (set/add/move/order/remove/clear or a class verb) and its argument
id-anchored: add/move carry after: <sibling id>|null; order([ids]) for a whole reorder; no fractional index, no tombstones
folder per page or session; JSONL per root with children inline; files.jsonl, settings.jsonl, inbox.jsonl, weight.jsonl beside it
per root file; growing collections partitioned by day (YYYY/MM/DD folders and day index files)
dev-only WebSocket JSON RPC with byte-offset resume plus loopback HTTP POST for writes; production = static fetch, read-only
full replay into a live object graph per file in each tab; one root per url; Node keeps up to 1,000 live roots
hand-rolled Events mixin: change/delta/read and list-verb events bubbling up parent links; views redraw on events
in-memory get(path)/find(id) via Maps; day indexes plus an in-memory query process; no database
full history kept forever in git; no snapshot line or compaction yet (designed); undo is app-level snapshots or git

Servex keeps one replayed root per file and advances it with each write
readers skip an unparseable line and the tailer waits for the newline, but Append.js/write_line glue the next line onto a torn tail
an unregistered type hydrates as a plain Item that keeps its wire name
no seq; cursor is a byte offset; order is file position
no merge, rebase or CRDT; optimistic tabs can diverge from the file
designed (snapshot line, page.<n>.jsonl), not built; Compact.mjs is dry-run only

lessons.why: Streaming layer: nine failing-test specs (run against the real code) for client op ids, retry-once, per-op acks, reset on rewritten logs, explicit ready, gap detection, presence, version handshake and reconnect, half-open detection; plus a seven-type message vocabulary.

Six gaps reproduced in node: a replayed line makes readers write (Ref re-path, auto-complete), one set() becomes one line per key, add drops child lists, an unset does not replay, after/type data collide, unknown verbs become data. Ranked fixes, op vocabulary, test specs.
